general.reason: The paper advertises a broad scope — the abstract says it generalizes to “spacetimes beyond inflation, including inhomogeneous and cyclic models,” and Sec. 3 says “we now consider arbitrary spacetimes without imposing FRW symmetry” — but the actual theorem is then restricted to “a geodesic congruence {u^\mu} with zero shear and vorticity \sigma_{\mu\nu}=\omega_{\mu\nu}=0.” That qualification materially narrows the claimed generality.

evidence.claim: The abstract and Sec. 3 claim to generalise to inhomogeneous spacetimes, but the proof requires zero shear and vorticity, excluding anisotropic and rotating models, so the claimed scope is overstated.
evidence.excerpt: the actual derivation (Sec. 3, between Eqs. 47 and 52) requires the geodesic congruence $\{u^\mu\}$ to have zero shear *and* zero vorticity, $\sigma_{\mu\nu}=\omega_{\mu\nu}=0$. This is essentially a hypersurface-orthogonal foliation assumption, which excludes Bianchi I anisotropic models, rotating cosmologies, and most genuinely inhomogeneous spacetimes. The result is still useful — but it is not a generalisation to “spacetimes beyond inflation, including inhomogeneous … models” in the unqualified sense the abstract advertises.

general.reason: The section title is “The Ijjas-Steinhardt Cyclic Model is Geodesically Incomplete,” but the proof is stated for a class of models: “We consider a universe with H(t) periodic with period T… Requiring that the Null Energy Condition holds everywhere except the bounce…” and concludes only that “Any spacetime periodic in H(t) and satisfying the condition (24) must therefore be geodesically incomplete.” The paper describes IS qualitatively (“In this model, the Hubble parameter… is periodic in time”), but does not explicitly verify all of these hypotheses for the IS construction itself.

evidence.claim: Sec. 2 claims to prove geodesic incompleteness for the Ijjas–Steinhardt model, but only proves a general result for periodic-H cyclic cosmologies and does not check whether the IS model satisfies all the stated hypotheses.
evidence.excerpt: Sec. 2 is titled “The Ijjas–Steinhardt Cyclic Model is Geodesically Incomplete”, but its content proves a general statement: any cosmology with periodic $H(t)$ satisfying the entropy-dissipation condition (Eq. 24) and NEC away from the bounce (Eq. 29) is past-incomplete. The Ijjas–Steinhardt model itself is invoked only in passing ... The paper does not explicitly verify that the Ijjas–Steinhardt construction satisfies the three hypotheses (periodicity of $H$, NEC away from the bounce, $\bar N > 0$) — this matters because the IS paper (Ref. 6) explicitly relies on a Horndeski/Galileon modification that violates the *null convergence* condition near the bounce, which is not the same as the NEC assumed here.
